rules.accepted_credit_types: Pharmacotherapeutics in a program beyond basic RN preparation, approved by the Board, prescriber-level and applicable to the scope of practice (or 1 academic credit hour); categories A-C up to 100%, D and E up to 20% (3 h); ACLS, PALS and CPR do not count
rules.alternatives: APRNs must keep current national certification; if a national certification lapses, that APRN license goes inactive. APRNs with independent prescriptive authority need 40 hours of Category I CME instead (may include the pharmacology hours if Category I).
rules.new_licensee_rule: Pharmacology documentation is not required when renewing within 24 months of initial prescriptive authority approval.
rules.audit_note: APRNs certify completion at renewal; if audited, submit certificates and course information (Form RS-24 may be used as a log).

topics.who: APRN-CNP, CNM and CNS with prescriptive authority under a supervising physician
APRNs with prescriptive authority holding a DEA registration: 2 h pain management or 2 h opioid use or addiction

rules.notes: Prescriptive authority renews with the 2-year RN and APRN license renewal. The 15 hours apply to APRNs with prescriptive authority; RN license CE rules apply separately.
rules.legal_basis: OAC 485:10-16-6 (as amended by 2025 emergency rules); 59 O.S. §567.4a(4)
rules.rule_quote: “Documentation verifying completion of a minimum of 15 contact hours or one academic hour of education, or the equivalent, in pharmacotherapeutics, clinical application, and use of pharmacological agents in the prevention of illness, and in the restoration and maintenance of health,…
